chapter_name: The Making of a Global World
learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the long history of globalization! See how the world shrank through ancient trade routes, disease, colonization, and the creation of modern global economies.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Globalization isn't new. For millennia, travelers, traders, and priests traveled vast distances. The 'Silk Routes' connected Asia with Europe and Africa. Foods like potatoes, tomatoes, and chilies traveled from the Americas to Europe and Asia. Even diseases traveled, like smallpox, which decimated Native Americans.

The world changed rapidly with three types of flows: trade (goods like cloth/wheat), labor (migration of people seeking work), and capital (investments). However, it also led to dark events, such as the spread of Rinderpest (cattle plague) which destroyed African livelihoods and forced them into colonial labor.

After WWI, mass production (pioneered by Henry Ford's assembly line) boosted economies briefly. But overproduction and fragile banking led to the Great Depression of 1929, causing massive global unemployment, ruined farmers, and shattered economies.

To prevent another Great Depression, global leaders met in Bretton Woods, USA (1944). They created the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank to stabilize global economies, launching the post-war era of globalization.

fun_activity.title: 🥔 The Potato Journey
fun_activity.instructions: Think of your favorite potato dish (French fries, Aloo Samosa). Did you know potatoes didn't exist in India or Europe 500 years ago? They came from South America! Next time you eat a potato, remember you are eating a product of global history.

exam_tips: 📌 The impact of 'Rinderpest' in Africa is a classic exam question. It shows how a simple cattle disease was used as a weapon of imperialism to force Africans into the labor market.
📌 Understand the concept of 'Indentured Labour' from India—it is often described as a 'new system of slavery'.
📌 The formation of the G-77 and their demand for a New International Economic Order (NIEO) is a crucial topic regarding post-WWII developing nations.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Silk Routes were vital pre-modern networks linking trade and culture globally.
⭐ 19th-century globalization brought economic growth to Europe but colonization to Asia and Africa.
⭐ The Bretton Woods institutions (IMF and World Bank) were established to manage the post-WWII global economy.
